title: Zerops Fundamentals: What Every Fresher Must Know
summary: Understand how Zerops works under the hood: Projects, Services, Build/Run Containers, and zerops.yml.

steps.title: What is Zerops and Why is it Different?
steps.content: Zerops is a developer-first platform-as-a-service (PaaS) built on bare-metal infrastructure and LXD/Linux containers. Unlike traditional serverless that suffers from cold starts, or raw VPS that requires tedious Docker & Linux maintenance, Zerops gives you dedicated containerized environments with automated CI/CD, auto-scaling, and managed databases without vendor lock-in.
steps.tip: Think of Zerops as having a senior DevOps engineer managing your container orchestration, SSL certificates, load balancers, and backups automatically.

steps.title: The Hierarchy: Project > Service > Container
steps.content:
In Zerops:
• **Project**: A logical grouping (e.g., 'My Ecommerce Store' or 'Portfolio App') containing all your backend, frontend, database, and cache services in a private isolated network.
• **Service**: An individual component like a Node.js API, a React Static frontend, a PostgreSQL database, or a Redis cache.
• **Container**: The lightweight, ultra-fast Linux environment where your code actually builds and executes.
steps.tip: Services inside the same project can talk to each other securely over internal hostnames without exposing databases to the public internet!

steps.title: The Brain: What is `zerops.yml`?
steps.content:
Every app deployed on Zerops is configured through a single file named `zerops.yml` placed in the root directory of your repository. It defines two main phases:
1. **Build Phase (prepare & build)**: Where you install dependencies (e.g., `npm install`, `pip install`) and compile assets (e.g., `npm run build`).
2. **Run Phase (run & deploy)**: Where you specify the runtime command (e.g., `npm start`, `python main.py`), port numbers, environment variables, and health checks.
steps.tip: Never forget to commit `zerops.yml` to your Git root directory before pushing!

steps.title: Deployment Triggers: Git vs zcli
steps.content:
You can deploy your code to Zerops in two primary ways:
• **GitHub / GitLab Auto-deploy**: Link your Git repository branch to Zerops service. Whenever you run `git push origin main`, Zerops automatically clones, builds, and deploys with zero downtime.
• **Zerops CLI (`zcli`)**: Push code directly from your local terminal with `zcli service push`, perfect for fast development testing without committing unfinished code.
steps.tip: Use `zcli` during hackathons or local testing, and connect GitHub for automated production CI/CD.

title: Your First Zerops Deployment: Complete Walkthrough
summary: From zero to live production URL in 5 practical steps.

steps.title: Create a Zerops Account & Project
steps.content:
1. Head to [app.zerops.io](https://app.zerops.io) and register with your email or GitHub.
2. In the dashboard, click **+ Add Project**.
3. Give your project a clear name like `fresher-demo-app` and select your preferred data center region (e.g., Frankfurt/Europe for lowest latency or closest to your users).
steps.tip: Projects organize related microservices. A single project can hold both frontend and backend.

steps.title: Create a Service in Your Project
steps.content:
Inside your new project:
1. Click **+ Add Service**.
2. Pick the service type matching your technology:
   - **Static** for React, Vite, Vue, HTML/CSS.
   - **Node.js** for Express, NestJS, Fastify.
   - **Python** for FastAPI, Django, Flask.
   - **PostgreSQL / MariaDB / Redis** for databases.
3. Enter a service hostname (e.g., `api` or `frontend`).
steps.tip: Choose container scaling mode: 'Auto-scaling' allows Zerops to scale RAM/CPU up during traffic spikes and down to save money!

steps.title: Add `zerops.yml` to Your Repository
steps.content:
Create `zerops.yml` in your code repository root. Make sure the `setup` key matches your service hostname (e.g., `api` or `app`).

```yaml
zerops:
  - setup: api
    build:
      base: nodejs@20
      buildCommands:
        - npm ci
      deployFiles:
        - dist
        - package.json
        - node_modules
    run:
      base: nodejs@20
      ports:
        - port: 3000
          httpSupport: true
      start: npm start
```
steps.tip: Always specify `httpSupport: true` if your service serves HTTP traffic to get an automatic HTTPS subdomain!

steps.title: Connect Git or Push via Zerops CLI
steps.content:
Option A (GitHub):
- In the Zerops service dashboard, click **Pipeline & CI/CD** -> **Connect Repository**.
- Select your GitHub repo and branch (`main`).

Option B (Zerops CLI):
- Install zcli: `npm install -g @zerops/zcli` or download binary.
- Log in: `zcli login <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>`
- Push: `zcli service push --service api`
steps.tip: Generate access tokens in Zerops -> User Avatar -> Access Tokens with Service: Push permission.

steps.title: Verify Deployment & Access Public URL
steps.content:
1. Watch the real-time build & deploy log stream in the Zerops dashboard.
2. Once the service transitions to the green **Running** state, enable public routing or click the generated `.zerops.app` subdomain.
3. Test your live endpoints via browser or curl!
steps.tip: Zerops automatically provisions free wildcard SSL (Let's Encrypt) certificates for all public subdomains and custom domains.

title: Mastering Environment Variables & Secrets
summary: How to securely configure API keys, database credentials, and cross-service links without exposing secrets.

steps.title: Why Never Commit .env Files to Git
steps.content: One of the most dangerous rookie mistakes is committing `.env` containing private API keys, Stripe secrets, or database passwords into GitHub. Zerops provides built-in Environment Variables management with AES-256 encryption.
steps.tip: Always add `.env` to your `.gitignore` file before running `git add .`!

steps.title: Setting Environment Variables in Zerops Dashboard
steps.content:
1. Navigate to your service in Zerops dashboard.
2. Click on **Environment Variables** in the left menu.
3. Add key-value pairs (e.g., `PORT=3000`, `NODE_ENV=production`, `JWT_SECRET=supersecret`).
4. Zerops securely injects these variables into your run container upon startup.
steps.tip: You can also specify default public environment variables inside `zerops.yml` under `run.envVariables`.

steps.title: Automatic Service Referencing (Cross-Service Links)
steps.content:
When you have a database service (e.g. `db`) and an API service (e.g. `api`) in the same project, Zerops automatically provides cross-service variables!
For example:
• `${db_hostname}` -> internal network hostname
• `${db_port}` -> internal port (e.g., 5432)
• `${db_user}` -> generated database username
• `${db_password}` -> secure database password
